why: The guard is pure policy: every branch of it is a decision about whether to touch somebody's cluster without asking first. It fails open in the worst direction — a mis-classified context proceeds silently — and not one of these edits produces an error message. They produce a missing question.

mutations.name: the context NAME check is dropped
mutations.breaks: Any context on loopback counts as local kind, so a docker-desktop or k3d cluster this repo never created is written to with no confirmation.

mutations.name: the API-server ADDRESS check is dropped
mutations.breaks: The name alone decides, and a name is cosmetic: a managed cluster whose context somebody called kind-prod is treated as local.

mutations.name: the confirmation is compared loosely
mutations.breaks: Any non-empty KAIMAHI_CONFIRM admits any context, so confirming one cluster becomes consent for the next — and the runbook tells operators to export that variable for a whole session.

mutations.name: a context missing from the kubeconfig is treated as present
mutations.breaks: The "about to be created" branch never runs, so `make up` on an empty machine — and every CI run — is classified remote and refused. The guard stops being usable, which is how a guard gets removed.

mutations.name: an unreadable kubeconfig is treated as an empty one
mutations.breaks: The guard cannot see where the context points and proceeds anyway: a kind-named context resolves to "not created yet" and is acted on without a question.
mutations.find:
echo "kube-guard: cannot read the kubeconfig — refusing to act blind." >&2
  exit 1

mutations.name: the no-TTY case proceeds instead of refusing
mutations.breaks: A script or CI job that reaches a remote context proceeds with nobody having agreed to it, precisely because there was nobody there to ask.
mutations.find:
echo "  to proceed:  KAIMAHI_CONFIRM=$CTX make <target>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

printf 'Type the context name to continue (anything else aborts): ' >&2
mutations.replace:
echo "  to proceed:  KAIMAHI_CONFIRM=$CTX make <target>" >&2
  exit 0
fi

printf 'Type the context name to continue (anything else aborts): ' >&2

mutations.name: the banner is not printed
mutations.breaks: The half of the contract that holds even when the guard proceeds: the operator is no longer told which cluster the action landed on.
